thag4.11:4.1: This is a difficult line. My reading depends on the speculative emending of the opening _tā_ to nominative plural, _te’matamada-_, agreeing with _bhekā_ in the next line. Then _matamada_ is “mad for the dead”, corresponding to the Sanskrit _mṛtamatta_, “jackal”. The commentary reads _amatamada_, “intoxicated by the deathless”, i.e. a snake, further explaining _amata_ here as _agada_, “antidote”. None of this strikes me as very likely. See Norman’s note 310 in *Elders Verses II* for further discussion. Perhaps the lines allude to the practice of the Saṅgha to recite chants dispelling snakes and other annoying creatures ([an4.67]()), suggesting that the frogs, too, benefit from this.
